method: Desktop mouse paths from the named starting state. Count each deliberate activation, including opening a native select and picking an option (2). Typing, waiting, automatic resolution, and site navigation are excluded and named where relevant. Reading at 0 means no click, hover, scroll, or keyboard shortcut. Decisions with several participants count each participant’s clicks. Repeated bids and edits add their own costs. Budgets are ceilings, not an instruction to remove safeguards.

criteria.name: Make each table piece feel like its job
criteria.rule: Reject three interchangeable status boxes or a generic pulse on every update. In settled desktop and phone captures, distinguish the seat pennant, ivory dice on felt, and torn paper receipt by shape and material, not just color. In a live rent handoff the dice land, the receipt posts, then the incoming player's pennant swings. Each cue settles within 600 ms without moving the text out of reach, delaying input, or looping at rest. No payment stamp for waived rent. With reduced motion or accents off, show the same faces, total, seats and amount without the cues.

criteria.name: Give different questions different places
criteria.rule: On a board with an interior, put the current decision maker, the previous roll and its roller, and the most recent payment in three separately labeled, non-overlapping places inside the circuit. At handoff a player must see who acts now and who just rolled and paid, without scrolling, opening history, or inferring it from color. Test after the incoming player's controls take their space, including on a short phone. Folded boards keep their compact result strip rather than reserving an empty middle.

criteria.name: Every persistent component earns its space
criteria.rule: Name the player task each always-visible component serves. If removing it leaves that task just as readable and reachable, remove it or move the explanation into Help. On the board, check that prints still identify districts without a permanent reference panel, normal play uses at most one line of footer, and trade help replaces that line only while a trade is open.

criteria.name: Read the deck without drawing
criteria.rule: A single selection on desktop or phone lists only the chosen space's public deck and explains each outcome, including movement, bills and detention. Inspection must not reveal the future, consume a card, or advance the game.

criteria.name: Every network member reprices
criteria.rule: Before buying a second airport, show the fare the buyer would collect at each airport. A bank sale or trade must preview the rate change on retained deeds, not just the price of the selected deed. Show a utility as a dice multiplier, never a guaranteed cash amount.

criteria.name: One ownership mark per deed
criteria.rule: A single horizontal mark must say both who owns the deed and how much of its district that seat owns. A complete set replaces the fraction, not the space around it. Unowned deeds have no mark. Keep ships and selection separate. Check a split district, a proposed swap, the accepted swap and a sale that breaks just one set. The same information must work without color, hovering or opening a panel.

criteria.name: Read a district from the whole deed
criteria.rule: District identity belongs to the tile face, not its header. With color and the top third excluded, the middle and lower face must still carry the district’s recognizable print. Names and values must remain legible on that print. Check every shipped map and the folded phone board, including intervening service spaces. Ownership and trade selections must not erase the print. A complete set must be readable without opening a portfolio, and its mark must disappear when the set breaks.

criteria.name: Show why this decision matters now
criteria.rule: When a deed is one player's last missing district member, an offer or auction must name that player and the rent at stake before the commitment, even if it is a rival. Before rolling, identify an almost complete district's missing deed and owner without a portfolio lookup. Show the real net-worth gap on a scored table; cash is not the score.

criteria.name: Read the result; never tidy it away
criteria.rule: The next turn must be playable while a letter still shows its recipient, instruction and actual effect. Allow a six-second read without input, on desktop and a muted reduced-motion phone. Then reclaim the chart automatically. One visit to Activity must recover the exact result, even after rejoin. Filing is not a game command and must not pause a bid clock.

criteria.name: Position is not ownership
criteria.rule: At rest, distinguish the owner of the occupied deed, the visiting ship and the owner's actual location without navigating, scrolling, hovering or relying on color. Test a visitor on a rival deed when the owner is somewhere else, plus several ships sharing a berth.

criteria.name: Board target and consequence visibility
criteria.rule: When a command targets deeds, mark the actual spaces and show cash and district effects before commitment. A board click selects, never spends or transfers. For trades, distinguish give, get, other owners and locked districts; reverse the viewpoint for the recipient and show both balances, sets made or broken and any lost refit. Test nondefault targets, refusal and both desktop and folded boards. Counting clicks alone is not a pass.
